16	id: https://chorus4ai.org/
17	name: CHoRUS Dataset
18	title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'
19	description: >-
20	  CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset generated by the
21	  Bridge2AI CHoRUS data generation project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded
22	  Bridge2AI consortium, under NIH award OT2OD032701. Data are collected retrospectively from
23	  intensive care admissions at contributing hospitals and are held under controlled access in a
24	  cloud enclave. The project website reports a currently released dataset of 50,000 patient
25	  admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, comprising 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized
26	  electronic health record data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data;
27	  a September 2025 training webinar instead reported over 45,000 unique admissions across 14
28	  hospitals as of August 2025. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9
29	  data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals, assembled by a consortium of more than 60
30	  members across 20 institutions. Nine data modalities are documented - demographics, medication
31	  administration (time-stamped at each infusion change or dose administration), procedures, nursing
32	  flowsheets (high-frequency documentation), diagnoses, clinical notes (extracted and tokenized with
33	  the OHNLP toolkit), imaging from PACS, waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and
34	  gateway/middleware, and waveform EEG from hospital databases. Structured EHR data and telemetry
35	  sit in the shared enclave; clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites with only
36	  tokens shared. The project also states an intention to sequester a holdout test set for external
37	  validation of models.

# D4D Datasheet for CHORUS Dataset
# Generation Method: schema-grounded agentic, phase 1
# Agent runtime: Claude API (direct)
# Provider: LBL CBORG (proxy to Anthropic)
# Model: claude-opus-5
# Mode: four-phase project agent, generic-v8 prompt
# Prompt: src/download/prompts/d4d_generic_arm_prompt_v8.md (identical for all projects)
# Arm: BASELINE (input documents only)
# Source bundle: data/preprocessed/concatenated/CHORUS_preprocessed.txt
# Source manifest: data/preprocessed/source_manifest.yaml
# Schema: src/data_sheets_schema/schema/data_sheets_schema_all.yaml
# Prior D4D factual reuse: prohibited
# Temperature: 0.0
# Generated: 2026-09-07

id: https://chorus4ai.org/
name: CHoRUS Dataset
title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'
description: >-
  CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset generated by the
  Bridge2AI CHoRUS data generation project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded
  Bridge2AI consortium, under NIH award OT2OD032701. Data are collected retrospectively from
  intensive care admissions at contributing hospitals and are held under controlled access in a
  cloud enclave. The project website reports a currently released dataset of 50,000 patient
  admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, comprising 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized
  electronic health record data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data;
  a September 2025 training webinar instead reported over 45,000 unique admissions across 14
  hospitals as of August 2025. The anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9
  data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals, assembled by a consortium of more than 60
  members across 20 institutions. Nine data modalities are documented - demographics, medication
  administration (time-stamped at each infusion change or dose administration), procedures, nursing
  flowsheets (high-frequency documentation), diagnoses, clinical notes (extracted and tokenized with
  the OHNLP toolkit), imaging from PACS, waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and
  gateway/middleware, and waveform EEG from hospital databases. Structured EHR data and telemetry
  sit in the shared enclave; clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites with only
  tokens shared. The project also states an intention to sequester a holdout test set for external
  validation of models.
notes: >-
  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."
status: Partially released under controlled access; acquisition, de-identification and curation continuing under NIH award OT2OD032701, whose project period runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.
page: https://chorus4ai.org/
created_by: CHoRUS Consortium
conforms_to: >-
  Structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication administration, procedures,
  nursing flowsheets, diagnoses) are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with published
  OMOP-schema metadata and OMOP schema extensions for nursing flowsheets; extracted and tokenized
  clinical notes follow the OHNLP open-source schema; imaging follows the DICOM schema; waveform
  telemetry follows WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema; waveform EEG follows the open-source
  EDF+ and Persyst schemas.
conforms_to_standard:
- OMOP_CDM
- DICOM
- WFDB
- OTHER
conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
conforms_to_class: Dataset
keywords:
- critical care
- acute illness
- intensive care unit
- electronic health records
- OMOP Common Data Model
- waveform telemetry
- electroencephalography
- medical imaging
- social determinants of health
- artificial intelligence
- machine learning
- Bridge2AI

  grants:
  - grant_number: OT2OD032701
    notes: >-
      Core project number OT2OD032701; project number for the funded application is
      1OT2OD032701-01, NIH application ID 10472824. Award amount 5,880,300 US dollars for fiscal
      year 2022; project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The awardee organization is Massachusetts
      General Hospital.

    The project website states that the content of the site is solely the responsibility of the
    authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the NIH.

purposes:
- response: >-
    To meet the need for generating data for machine learning and artificial intelligence
    applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications,
    and measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    To develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods used
    promote privacy, accountability and clinical benefit.
- response: >-
    To provision a holdout test set accessible for external validation of models, aiding marketplace
    adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
- response: >-
    To create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and to create best
    practices for AI in health, as one of four data generation projects in the Bridge2AI consortium.
- response: >-
    To develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready dataset addressing the
    grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.

tasks:
- response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
- response: Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    External validation of machine learning models against a sequestered holdout dataset.
- response: >-
    Labeling data with targets important for prediction, using a visualization and annotation
    environment.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine
    learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center datasets is described as a
    critical first step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
- response: >-
    Existing resources lack a diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready critical care
    dataset able to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
- response: >-
    Multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging and text data are not harmonized across centers; CHoRUS
    develops unified standards to harmonize them.
- response: >-
    Sequestered holdout data for independent external validation of clinical AI models are scarce,
    which the project addresses by sequestering holdout datasets.

    Published metadata follows the OHNLP open-source schema; as of August 2025 the metadata entry
    for this modality was marked planned.
- instance_type: Admission with radiology imaging data obtained from hospital PACS
  counts: 7642
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15
  notes: >-
    The project website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released
    dataset. Imaging follows the DICOM schema; metadata was marked planned as of August 2025.
  source_caveats: >-
    The two sources count different units and were both retained rather than reconciled: the project
    website (tier 2) reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data, while the cohort 2 webinar
    (tier 4) states that as of August 2025 imaging was "currently 1000 images available with de-id
    in process for larger cohort".
- instance_type: Waveform telemetry recording from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
  notes: >-
    Stored in WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema. The project website reports 23 Tb of waveform
    data in the current released dataset.
- instance_type: Waveform EEG recording from hospital EEG databases
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
  notes: >-
    Stored as EDF+ and Persyst; extraction was in process as of August 2025 and the metadata entry
    was marked planned.

subpopulations:
- subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Released admissions are identified by care setting as adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric
    intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) admissions.
  source_caveats: The bundle does not report the distribution of admissions across these settings.

splits:
- split_details: >-
    The award abstract states that the dataset will also provision a holdout test set, accessible
    for model external validation to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models, and describes
    sequestering holdout datasets for external validation.
  source_caveats: >-
    Stated as a project intention in the 2022 award abstract; the bundle does not state the size,
    composition or availability of the holdout set.

acquisition_methods:
- acquisition_details: >-
    Retrospective collection: clinical data generated during routine care are extracted at
    contributing hospitals, standardized, tokenized, stored, visualized and labeled through a
    multi-center network, then delivered as a CHoRUS data extract to the shared cloud enclave.

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    Extraction of structured electronic health record data at contributing sites and standardization
    to the OMOP Common Data Model, supported by the OHDSI tool stack.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Extraction of clinical notes and tokenization using the OHNLP toolkit; note text remains at the
    site and only tokens are shared.
- mechanism_details: Retrieval of imaging studies from hospital PACS in DICOM form.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Capture of waveform telemetry from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware, converted to WFDB
    using the waveform conversion scripts maintained in the chorus_waveform repository.
- mechanism_details: Extraction of EEG waveforms from hospital EEG databases as EDF+ and Persyst.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Site-side tooling for building and delivering submissions, including the chorus-extract-upload
    tools to create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract and dockerized container applications deployed
    to support CHoRUS services on Azure.

collection_timeframes:
- timeframe_details: >-
    Data collection is retrospective. As of August 2025 the assembled dataset covered 14 different
    hospitals. The funded project period runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not state the calendar range of the clinical encounters represented in the data;
    the dates given are the award project period and the August 2025 status snapshot.

data_collectors:
- collector_details: >-
    Fourteen data acquisition centers, drawn from a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers,
    contribute clinical data extracts. Site data managers follow the step-by-step extraction and
    contribution workflow documented in the Chorus_SOP repository and report progress through
    regular status updates.
  role: Data contributing sites
- collector_details: >-
    CHoRUS sub-teams for Standards, Data Acquisition and Tooling support extraction, mapping and
    delivery and maintain the recordings and documentation referenced from the workflow diagram.
  role: Consortium sub-teams

direct_collection:
- is_direct: false
  collection_details: >-
    Data are obtained retrospectively from hospital clinical systems - electronic health records,
    PACS, bedside monitor gateways and hospital EEG databases - at contributing centers, rather than
    collected directly from individuals for research purposes.

sampling_strategies:
- strategies: >-
    Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies,
    within a legal framework established for collecting data at scale. Federated access enabling
    sampling methods intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort.
  notes: >-
    The project states an aim of assembling the most diverse dataset addressing recovery from acute
    illness; the bundle does not describe the sampling frame or selection criteria in operational
    detail.

raw_data_sources:
- source_description: Structured electronic health record systems at 14 data contributing hospitals
  source_type: Hospital electronic health record
  raw_data_format: Site-native EHR extracts mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model
- source_description: Unstructured clinical notes held in hospital electronic health record systems
  source_type: Hospital electronic health record
  raw_data_format: Free text, extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit
  access_details: Note text is stored locally at the contributing site; only tokens are placed in the shared enclave.
- source_description: Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS)
  source_type: Clinical imaging archive
  raw_data_format: DICOM
- source_description: Bedside physiologic monitors and their gateway/middleware
  source_type: Clinical monitoring device stream
  raw_data_format: Waveform telemetry converted to WFDB
- source_description: Hospital EEG databases
  source_type: Clinical neurophysiology database
  raw_data_format: EDF+ and Persyst

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Standardization of structured EHR data to the OMOP Common Data Model, using validated semantic
    mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled
    tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Extraction and tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP
    toolkit.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, including de-identification
    of imaging, which was in process for the larger imaging cohort as of August 2025.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Conversion of waveform telemetry into WFDB using the waveform conversion scripts and preparation
    resources maintained for waveform release.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using the open source UF-Geocoding code
    maintained in the chorus-ai GitHub organization.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data
    submissions, and site status tracking is used to identify and resolve blocking issues in the
    creation and curation of a site's data extract.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    The project states that a visualization and annotation environment will label data with targets
    important for prediction, and that it will develop capabilities across the multi-center network
    to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize and label data.
  data_annotation_protocol: >-
    Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping and validation under a clinical validation
    SOP associated with the chorus-mapping repository.
  source_caveats: >-
    The annotation environment is described in the future tense in the award abstract and the GitHub
    organization overview; the bundle does not report labels present in the released data.

machine_annotation_tools:
- tools:
  - OHNLP toolkit
  tool_descriptions: >-
    Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized automatically using the OHNLP toolkit, and the
    resulting tokens are published against the OHNLP open-source schema.

missing_data_documentation:
- missing_data_patterns: >-
    Modality coverage was uneven at the August 2025 snapshot: OMOP data and telemetry were in the
    enclave, clinical notes were stored locally with only tokens shared, roughly 1,000 images were
    available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was still in
    process. Published metadata existed for demographics, medication administration, procedures,
    nursing flowsheets, diagnoses and waveform telemetry, while metadata for clinical notes, imaging
    and EEG was marked planned.
  missing_data_causes: >-
    De-identification, extraction and metadata publication workflows for imaging, EEG and clinical
    notes were still in progress.

is_deidentified:
  method: >-
    Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; unstructured EHR text is
    tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit rather than shared as free text; imaging de-identification was
    in process as of August 2025.
  deidentification_details: >-
    Clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens placed in the shared
    enclave, so that identifiable narrative text is not distributed with the dataset.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not enumerate the identifiers removed, name a de-identification standard, or
    report residual re-identification risk. A privacy scan tool for medical records and a CTP-deid
    repository exist in the chorus-ai GitHub organization, but the bundle does not state that either
    was applied to the released data.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The dataset consists of hospital records of critically ill patients, including demographics,
    diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, imaging, physiologic
    waveforms, EEG and tokenized clinical notes.
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    Social determinants of health, which the unified standards are to harmonize, and contextual
    factors that the award abstract states data elements will feature, such as geographic distance
    to the nearest hospital.

confidential_elements:
- confidential_elements_present: true
  confidentiality_details: >-
    Clinical note text is confidential to the contributing site: it is stored locally and is not
    placed in the shared enclave, which receives only tokens.
- confidential_elements_present: true
  confidentiality_details: >-
    Every documented modality is marked as controlled for access control; the dataset is not openly
    downloadable.

participant_privacy:
- anonymization_method: >-
    Tokenization of unstructured EHR text, de-identification of imaging, and transformation of data
    using approaches that limit re-identification.
  privacy_techniques: >-
    Local retention of clinical note text at contributing sites, with only tokens shared. Controlled
    access to all modalities within a cloud enclave.
  notes: >-
    Patient-focused work within the consortium determines the ethical and legal approaches used to
    manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.

human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: true
  regulatory_compliance:
  - >-
    The project establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing
    legal and regulatory landscape as part of its ethics work.
  special_populations:
  - >-
    Released admissions include pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU)
    patients.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the
    dataset.

at_risk_populations:
  at_risk_groups_included: true
  source_caveats: >-
    Inclusion of minors follows from the released dataset covering PICU and NICU admissions; the
    bundle describes no assent procedures, guardian consent procedures or special protections.

ethical_reviews:
- review_details: >-
    The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate
    for public sharing.
  source_caveats: >-
    Described in the award abstract as project ethics activity; the bundle names no institutional
    review board, ethics committee or reviewing organization for the dataset.
- review_details: >-
    The consortium evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase
    trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI, developing new approaches as the existing legal
    and regulatory landscape is analyzed.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Imaging coverage was partial at the August 2025 snapshot, with roughly 1,000 images available
    and de-identification in process for a larger cohort.
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    EEG data extraction was still in process as of August 2025, so EEG coverage of the released
    admissions was incomplete.
- limitation_type: integration_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are available in the
    shared enclave, so analyses requiring full note text cannot be performed on the shared data.
- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Data come from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers and
    cover acute and critical care admissions only, so the population is not a general hospital or
    general population sample.
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The released dataset of 50,000 admissions is smaller than the anticipated final dataset of
    100,000 patient admissions, and modality-level metadata publication was incomplete.
  scope_impact: >-
    Analyses run on the current release may not generalize to the completed dataset, whose
    composition across modalities is expected to change.
  source_caveats: >-
    The comparison between the released and anticipated admission counts is this record's own
    juxtaposition of the two figures the project website states (50,000 and 100,000); neither source
    states a completion fraction.

license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    Access to the dataset is controlled. Participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care
    Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before
    gaining access to the dataset.
  notes: >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub organization states that its project is licensed under the MIT License,
    with individual repositories carrying MIT or Apache-2.0; this covers CHoRUS software and tooling
    rather than the clinical dataset.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle states the licensing agreement requirement only in the context of the training
    program registration flow and does not reproduce the agreement or name a data use license for
    the dataset itself.

data_governance:
  accountable_organization:
    name: Massachusetts General Hospital
  access_review_process: >-
    All modalities are under controlled access. Access requests are directed to named CHoRUS
    contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org). For the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI
    for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form giving name, email
    and institution and sign the licensing agreement included in that form; once access is granted
    and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant. A ".edu" email address is
    required to gain access to the dataset, and program administrators assist with this access where
    needed.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle names access contacts but does not name a data access committee, its membership, an
    access decision timeframe, or an appeal process. Massachusetts General Hospital is recorded as
    accountable organization because it is the awardee organization for OT2OD032701 and hosts the
    program manager; the bundle does not use the term data steward.

regulatory_restrictions:
  confidentiality_level: restricted
  regulatory_restrictions:
  - >-
    All nine documented data types are marked as controlled for access control, and access requires
    a signed licensing agreement and an institutional (".edu") email address. Data are worked with
    inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files.
  source_caveats: >-
    The bundle does not state HIPAA, GDPR or export-control determinations for the dataset; HIPAA
    and GDPR compliance appear only as topics of a training workshop on IRB, data compliance and
    quality assurance.

distribution_formats:
- format: OMOP Common Data Model relational tables
  notes: >-
    Demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets and diagnoses, with
    published metadata against the OMOP schema (with extensions for nursing flowsheets).
- format: OHNLP open-source schema (tokenized clinical notes)
  notes: >-
    Notes are extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit; note text remains stored locally at
    contributing sites and only tokens are shared. Metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.
- format: DICOM
  notes: Imaging obtained from PACS; metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.
- format: WFDB
  notes: Waveform telemetry from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware, documented against an extended PhysioNet schema.
- format: EDF+ and Persyst
  notes: Waveform EEG from hospital databases, documented against the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas; metadata publication was planned as of August 2025.

third_party_sharing:
- is_shared: true
  notes: >-
    The dataset is made available beyond the contributing centers under controlled access. The
    AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program is described as expanding access to
    Bridge2AI CHoRUS data; its Cohort 2, announced for November 17, 2025 through July 31, 2026, will
    select up to 30 trainees who work with the data on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care
    Collaborative Cloud after signing the licensing agreement.

existing_uses:
- examples:
  - As of August 2025, the datasets are being used for training activities and publications.
- examples:
  - >-
    Characterization reports are produced from site submissions and returned to the contributing
    sites (CHoRUSReports).

intended_uses:
- use_category: Clinical AI/ML model development
  examples:
  - Building machine learning and AI models to characterize acute and critical care illness
  - Predicting complications and deterioration in patients with acute or critical illness
  - Measuring treatment response
  usage_notes: >-
    The project's stated aim is to build ML- and AI-derived models that improve the care and
    outcomes of patients requiring critical care.
- use_category: External validation of clinical AI models
  examples:
  - Evaluating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset
  usage_notes: >-
    Intended to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and
    critical care.
- use_category: Workforce training and AI literacy
  examples:
  - Hands-on trainee research on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud
  - Canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP common data model workshops and clinical deep learning exercises
  usage_notes: >-
    The project cultivates expertise in the lay and scientific community to improve AI literacy and
    utilization through multimodal educational approaches.

other_tasks:
- task_details: >-
    Analyses incorporating social determinants of health, which the project accounts for in its
    patient-focused ethical and legal work and harmonizes through its unified standards.

future_use_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    The sequestered holdout set is intended to support external validation and thereby aid
    marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
- impact_details: >-
    Because the data derive from critically ill patients, the project frames privacy, accountability
    and clinical benefit as conditions on future use, with patient-focused work determining the
    ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants
    of health.
- impact_details: >-
    Community perspectives gathered through ethics focus groups determine what data is appropriate
    for public sharing, so the shareable scope of future releases depends on those findings.

maintainers:
- maintainer_details: >-
    Ciera McCrary, Program Manager, Massachusetts General Hospital, listed as the project contact on
    the CHoRUS website (cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu, address as printed on the site).
  role: academic_institution
- maintainer_details: >-
    Access requests are handled by dbold@emory.edu and by Jared Houghtaling
    (jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org), listed as the contacts of the chorus-ai organization.
  role: academic_institution
- maintainer_details: >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub organization maintains 28 repositories of CHoRUS software and documentation;
    versions, maintainers and other package metadata are tracked on a package status page, with
    contributor and user documentation compiled in the chorus-developer repository.
  role: other

updates:
  update_details: >-
    The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient
    admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of August 2025,
    de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process, and metadata
    publication for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was planned.
  source_caveats: The bundle does not state an update frequency or a versioning policy.

extension_mechanism:
  contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai
  extension_details: >-
    Contributing sites submit regular status updates on their extraction and curation progress,
    either through the GitHub interface directly or through a Google Form whose submissions update
    GitHub status and issue information automatically; these statuses feed the Standards Project and
    the Data Acquisition Project. Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping through the
    chorus-mapping repository under a clinical validation SOP. Problems encountered in creating or
    submitting a data extract are posted in the Standards Discussions or Data Acquisition
    Discussions.

external_resources:
- external_resources:
  - >-
    CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/), with pages on the team, project overview, tools,
    data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset and learning resources.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai), 28 public repositories providing
    software and tooling for clinical data, validated semantic mappings, standard operating protocols
    for contributing sites, and project management overviews.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    Chorus_SOP - centralized SOP documentation site with an interactive workflow diagram describing
    the step-by-step process for extracting and contributing clinical data to CHoRUS.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus-mapping - documentation and pooled tabular mappings with an associated clinical validation
    SOP for contributing to mapping efforts.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources - waveform documentation, conversion scripts, and
    resources supporting the preparation and release of waveforms.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    chorus-extract-upload - tools to create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract; chorus-container-apps -
    dockerized container applications and configurations deployed to support CHoRUS services on Azure.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    privacy_scan_tool - a privacy scan tool for medical records; CTP-deid; UF-Geocoding - open source
    code to geocode OMOP Location entities via DeGauss.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    CHoRUSReports - repository producing characterization reports returned to sites following their
    data submissions.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    Bridge2AI project page for CHoRUS (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) and the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for
    Clinical Care training program call for applications hosted on AIM-AHEAD.net.

source_caveats: >-
  Four sources were used, ranked: the CHoRUS project website (project_documentation, tier 2), the
  NIH RePORTER project page for OT2OD032701 (tier 4), the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care
  Cohort 2 informational webinar of September 2025 (tier 4), and a 2025-11-14 capture of the
  chorus-ai GitHub organization overview (tier 5). The 2022 award abstract is written in the future
  tense about project plans and is recorded here as intention rather than as current dataset state.
  Volume figures differ between the tier-2 website (50,000 released admissions) and the tier-4
  webinar (over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025); the higher-ranked figure is stated with
  the disagreement noted at the affected instance. The webinar's imaging figure (1,000 images) and
  the website's (7,642 admissions with radiology data) count different units and are both retained.
  The 23 Tb waveform figure is reported for waveform data only, so no dataset-wide size is recorded.
  The cohort 2 webinar lists six people under the heading "Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team" with
  institutions but no individual role descriptions; only Eric Rosenthal is independently attested as
  principal investigator, by the NIH RePORTER project page, and principal_investigator is the only
  person-valued field the Creator class declares, so it carries each listed leader. The bundle
  states that CHoRUS is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and collaborates with the
  other three, but names no sibling dataset, so no dataset relationships are recorded.

2	"""
3	Validate D4D evaluation JSON files against their schemas.
4	
5	This ensures evaluations conform to the standardized schema, which in turn
6	ensures HTML renderers can reliably parse the output.
7	"""
8	import argparse
9	import json
10	import re as _re
11	import sys
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
14	
15	try:
16	    import jsonschema
17	    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
18	except ImportError:
19	    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
20	    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
21	    sys.exit(1)
22	
23	
24	def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
25	    """Load JSON Schema file."""
26	    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
27	        return json.load(f)
28	
29	
30	def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
31	    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
32	    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
33	        return json.load(f)
34	
35	
36	#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
37	#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
38	#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
39	#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
40	#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
41	SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")
42	
43	
44	def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
45	    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.
46	
47	    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.
48	
49	    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
50	    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
51	    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
52	    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
53	    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
54	    """
55	    errors = []
56	    try:
57	        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
58	        return "valid", []
59	    except ValidationError as e:
60	        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
61	        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
62	        if e.schema_path:
63	            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
64	        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
65	            return "superseded", errors
66	        return "invalid", errors
67	
68	
69	def validate_evaluation(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
70	    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
71	    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)
72	    return status == "valid", errors
73	
74	
75	def validate_outputs(paths: List[Path], rubric: str | None = None,
76	                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
77	    """Require each explicitly named new output to pass its semantic schema.
78	
79	    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
80	    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
81	    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
82	    """
83	    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"
84	    names = {"rubric10-semantic": "rubric10_semantic_schema.json",
85	             "rubric20-semantic": "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"}
86	    failed = not paths
87	    for path in paths:
88	        try:
89	            doc = load_evaluation(path)
90	            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
91	                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
92	            declared = doc.get("rubric")
93	            if not isinstance(declared, str) or declared not in names:
94	                raise ValueError(f"no semantic evaluation schema for rubric {declared!r}")
95	            if rubric is not None and declared != rubric:
96	                raise ValueError(f"expected {rubric}, found {declared}")
97	            valid, errors = validate_evaluation(doc, load_schema(schema_dir / names[declared]))
98	            if not valid:
99	                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
100	        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
101	            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
102	            failed = True
103	        else:
104	            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
105	    return int(failed)
106	
107	
108	#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
109	#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
110	#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
111	#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
112	#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
113	KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")
114	
115	
116	def is_kept(path: Path, base: Path) -> bool:
117	    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
118	    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])
119	
120	
121	def discover(base: Path) -> List[Path]:
122	    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.
123	
124	    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
125	    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
126	    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
127	    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
128	    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
129	    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
130	    not have to.
131	    """
132	    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))
133	
134	
135	def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
136	    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.
137	
138	    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
139	    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
140	    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
141	    """
142	    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
143	    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
144	    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"
145	
146	    schemas = {
147	        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
148	        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
149	    }
150	
151	    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
152	    if not eval_files:
153	        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
154	        return 1
155	
156	    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")
157	
158	    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
159	    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
160	    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
161	    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
162	    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
163	
164	    for eval_file in eval_files:
165	        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
166	        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
167	        try:
168	            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
169	            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
170	                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
171	        except Exception as e:
172	            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
173	            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
174	            continue
175	
176	        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
177	        if rubric not in schemas:
178	            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
179	            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
180	            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
181	            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
182	            continue
183	
184	        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
185	        counts[(where, status)] += 1
186	        if status == "invalid":
187	            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
188	        elif status == "superseded":
189	            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")
190	
191	    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
192	        for shown, errors in rows:
193	            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
194	            for error in errors:
195	                print(f"     {error}")
196	
197	    print()
198	    print("=" * 60)
199	    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
200	    for where in ("live", "kept"):
201	        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
202	        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
203	              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
204	    if no_schema:
205	        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
206	              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
207	    print("=" * 60)
208	
209	    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
210	    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
211	    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
212	    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
213	    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1
214	
215	
216	def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
217	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
218	    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
219	                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
220	    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
221	                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
222	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
223	    if args.rubric and not args.files:
224	        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
225	    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()
226	
227	
228	if __name__ == "__main__":
229	    sys.exit(cli())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Validate D4D evaluation JSON files against their schemas.

This ensures evaluations conform to the standardized schema, which in turn
ensures HTML renderers can reliably parse the output.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re as _re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

try:
    import jsonschema
    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
    sys.exit(1)


def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load JSON Schema file."""
    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")


def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.

    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.

    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
    """
    errors = []
    try:
        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
        return "valid", []
    except ValidationError as e:
        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
        if e.schema_path:
            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
            return "superseded", errors
        return "invalid", errors


def validate_evaluation(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)
    return status == "valid", errors


def validate_outputs(paths: List[Path], rubric: str | None = None,
                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Require each explicitly named new output to pass its semantic schema.

    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
    """
    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"
    names = {"rubric10-semantic": "rubric10_semantic_schema.json",
             "rubric20-semantic": "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"}
    failed = not paths
    for path in paths:
        try:
            doc = load_evaluation(path)
            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
            declared = doc.get("rubric")
            if not isinstance(declared, str) or declared not in names:
                raise ValueError(f"no semantic evaluation schema for rubric {declared!r}")
            if rubric is not None and declared != rubric:
                raise ValueError(f"expected {rubric}, found {declared}")
            valid, errors = validate_evaluation(doc, load_schema(schema_dir / names[declared]))
            if not valid:
                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
            failed = True
        else:
            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
    return int(failed)


#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")


def is_kept(path: Path, base: Path) -> bool:
    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])


def discover(base: Path) -> List[Path]:
    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.

    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
    not have to.
    """
    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))


def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.

    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
    """
    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"

    schemas = {
        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
    }

    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
    if not eval_files:
        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
        return 1

    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")

    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

    for eval_file in eval_files:
        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
        try:
            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
            continue

        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
        if rubric not in schemas:
            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
            continue

        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
        counts[(where, status)] += 1
        if status == "invalid":
            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
        elif status == "superseded":
            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")

    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
        for shown, errors in rows:
            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
            for error in errors:
                print(f"     {error}")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
    for where in ("live", "kept"):
        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
    if no_schema:
        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
    print("=" * 60)

    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1


def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.rubric and not args.files:
        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(cli())

Validation passed with exit status 0.

## Definition check

The "Reproducibility" section is present in my instructions and reads as expected of the current rules. The sentence beginning "Repeatability must be", verbatim and in full:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

## Evaluation written

`output_evaluation.json` — CHORUS, `claudecode_api`, rep3. Validated: `VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic`.

**Score: 65 / 88 — fixed 73.9%, normalized 73.9%** (denominators identical: all four "Applies to" trigger conditions were satisfied, so `excluded_max_points: 0`, `adjusted_max_points: 88`, `questions_not_applicable: 0`). Every question carries `applicable: true`; no null scores.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| Structural Completeness (Q1–5) | 19 / 21 |
| Metadata Quality & Content (Q6–10) | 17 / 21 |
| Technical Documentation (Q11–15) | 16 / 25 |
| FAIRness & Accessibility (Q16–20) | 13 / 21 |

**Applicability, resolved before scoring (anti-circular rule).** Each conditional question records `applicability_evidence` drawn from fields belonging to *other* questions: Q8/Q15 from description, keywords and collection_mechanisms; Q11 from external_resources' code repositories plus purposes' "tools around artificial intelligence"; Q10/Q17 from third_party_sharing and the access-review process, applying the ambiguity rule so approval-gated access counts as shared; Q12/Q13 from the populated collection fields plus that sharing condition. No question's own fields were used to exclude it.

**What drove the score.** Strengths are real: tier-ranked source provenance with disclosed conflicts, per-modality standards conformance (OMOP/DICOM/WFDB/EDF+/OHNLP) that is technically correct, a valid NIH grant (OT2OD032701 parses correctly — OT2 activity code, OD institute), and a confidentiality architecture propagated consistently across nine fields.

The deductions are mostly semantic rather than presence-based. Sixteen issues are recorded, four of them high severity: `involves_human_subjects=true` with no named IRB and no informed consent or waiver; no known_biases field in a record titled "…for Equitable AI"; and no version, version_access, errata or DOI for a dataset the record itself describes as growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions. Consistency checks: 20 passed, 5 failed, 7 warnings. Note one cascade — the absent persistent identifier caps Q6, Q13, Q14 and Q19 together, and the absent demographics (Q15) makes the Q20 fairness analysis structurally impossible.

Two serialization notes, for transparency. The first write failed validation on unescaped quotes inside two evidence strings (`".edu"`); I fixed the escaping only — no judgement was altered to satisfy the validator. Second, `evaluation_timestamp` is `2026-09-12T15:46:06Z`, derived from the pinned record's filesystem timestamp because this sandbox denied the clock commands; treat it as session-dated rather than instant-accurate. Model recorded as `claude-opus-5` for both `name` and `evaluator_model` per the launcher's canonical identifier, `temperature: null`.
